source_review.notes: Checked all fourteen references. Kubernetes large-cluster, API Priority and Fairness, API/watch, controller, metrics, and admission behavior; etcd hardware, performance, maintenance, and monitoring; Google SRE overload/cascading/load guidance; and HTTP 429 semantics were reviewed against current official documentation. Version-sensitive claims are qualified and the etcd references use the current stable documentation line.

evidence: Reviewed cost-class arrival, admission/completion, service demand, parallel capacity, headroom, queue age, retry/fan-out, utilization, Little's Law, and recovery-drain notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates original intent from attempts and admission from useful completion, and labels the linear utilization form as a planning approximation.

evidence: Executed ten synthetic scenarios and reproduced qualified=5 with one each API, store, provider, nonconvergent recovery, and critical-starvation failure.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The six mutually exclusive first-failure categories total ten and apply a 25 percent headroom boundary consistently.

evidence: Verified utilization dimension, Little's Law boundary requirements, retry/fan-out amplification, recovery-drain positivity condition, and min(na,e) shared-store bound.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The recovery equation correctly becomes nonconvergent when completion does not exceed new arrivals.

evidence: Reviewed large lists/objects, watch reconnect, cold cache, retry storm, slow disk, etcd space, admission slowdown, provider throttle, tenant bulk action, broad APF exemption, zone loss, maintenance, upgrade, telemetry loss, and full restore.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage includes steady, burst, adversarial, degraded, failure-domain, maintenance, and recovery envelopes.

evidence: Traced admission, critical-progress, client, state-store, and recovery invariants through API, queue, controller, extension, storage, provider, load-shedding, and restoration examples.
invariant_checking.notes: Each invariant states a measurable capacity or correctness boundary rather than a component resource target.

evidence: Verified the shared-store counterexample: n stateless replicas of capacity a remain bounded by min(na,e) when all writes require store capacity e.
proof_review.notes: The conclusion correctly extends only as an analogous bottleneck pattern and requires end-to-end empirical qualification.

evidence: The replica-scaling argument is explicitly labeled a proof sketch with premise, bound, saturation consequence, possible negative overhead, and scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No Kubernetes or vendor throughput number is claimed as a theorem.

evidence: The executable capacity audit is explicitly synthetic and disclaims production sizing; illustrative demand and utilization figures are scenario data; current sources are retrieval-dated.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No real benchmark, certified cluster limit, platform capacity, recovery time, control effectiveness, or external review is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed work graphs/classes, demand envelopes, queueing, API clients, controllers, fairness, extensions, state store, watches/caches, workflows/providers, headroom, shedding, testing, forecasting, and client migration.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementability with attributed client budgets, shared watches, keyed queues, APF classification, extension latency budgets, etcd maintenance, provider token budgets, production-shaped load/fault tests, recovery qualification, and versioned safe envelopes.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified required order, one-page review, definitions/notation, twelve-step mechanism, five invariants, bounded proof sketch, eighteen trade-offs, thirty misconceptions, ten examples, ten connections, fourteen references, and five answered exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
